Senses.Explanation: Right then and there: a temporal expression marking something as occurring without an intervening interval. Shanglan Shun's verse says accumulated ignorance disappears right then; the Five Lamps narrator says Zhitian awakens on the spot when shown the blowing-a-hair case. Huangbo Xiyun uses it for the time of becoming clear without retaining a mark of clarity, while Linji Yixuan uses it for being without further business after turning the light back and recognizing no difference from the patriarchs and buddhas. Huqiu Shaolong says that if listeners trust the presented mind-settling scene, the mind is settled right then. Wuyi Yuanlai attaches the expression to one thought not arising, Miyin to the ice-like disappearance of a raised repentance case, Xuedou Chongxian to a mirror distinguishing beautiful and ugly as soon as it is set up, and the Yongzheng Emperor to a selected saying and discriminating consciousness shattering on the spot. The Zen record prizes the compressed timing, but the word itself remains a temporal modifier: it does not by itself name a teaching, a prescribed exercise, or a distinct temporal entity.
Senses.Note: Frozen-corpus concordance: 1,568 exact hits in 319 files and 315 independent works. Verbal, verse, and narrative uses all mark immediate timing. English noun phrases such as 'the present' are excluded from the preferred gloss because the curated evidence consistently modifies events or states rather than naming a distinct temporal object.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若能如此全知曉，塵劫無明當下消。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Full Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Shanglan Shun section. The record explicitly introduces this among Shanglan Shun's instruction verses; Shanglan is the exact verse speaker saying accumulated ignorance disappears right then.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一日，室中示吹布毛因緣，師當下開悟
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Full Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Zhenjue Zhitian biography. The Five Lamps compiler narrates that Zhitian awakened on the spot when shown the blowing-a-hair case; the statement is not Zhitian's own speech.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The headword modifies a third-person biographical report of Zhenjue Zhitian's awakening; it is not quoted speech by Zhitian.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Wanling Record of Huangbo Xiyun. Huangbo Xiyun is the exact speaker saying that at the time one becomes clear right then, one must not retain a mark of clarity.

Occurrences.Kwic: 知身心與祖佛不別當下無事方名得法
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Linji Yixuan record. Linji Yixuan is the exact speaker placing being without further business right then after turning back and knowing body and mind are not different from patriarchs and buddhas.

Continuation of the Orthodox Lamp Lineage (續燈正統), Huqiu Shaolong section. In his own hall address, Huqiu Shaolong is the exact speaker saying that if listeners can trust the presented scene, the mind is settled right then.
Extensive Record of Chan Master Wuyi Yuanlai (無異元來禪師廣錄), Boshan hall address. Wuyi Yuanlai is the exact speaker attaching right-then timing to one thought not arising.

Occurrences.Kwic: 復被山僧一喝，當下冰消而去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Miyin of Guangfushan Shengjue Monastery (廣福山勝覺寺密印禪師語錄), hall address. Miyin is the exact speaker saying that the raised repentance case disappears like ice on the spot after his shout.

Occurrences.Kwic: 明鏡忽臨臺，當下分妍醜。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Pointing at the Moon Record (指月錄), Buddha-and-outsider case. The compilation explicitly introduces Xuedou Chongxian's verse; Xuedou is the exact historical verse speaker saying that when a bright mirror reaches the stand it distinguishes beautiful and ugly on the spot.

Occurrences.Kwic: 并此無義味語，一時忘却，當下百雜粉碎
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄), imperially authored preface. The Yongzheng Emperor writes in his own first-person preface that when even the meaningless saying is forgotten, the mass of discriminations shatters on the spot.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The imperially authored preface identifies the Yongzheng Emperor as the writer of this headword-bearing sentence; he is a named non-master author.
